title: The Mystery of the Death Valley Germans
summary: Hosts examine the 1996 disappearance of the Death Valley Germans: Egbert Rimkus, Cornelia "Connie" Meyer, her son Max and Egbert's son George, who vanished during a three-week California and Nevada road trip. Their abandoned Plymouth Voyager minivan was found stuck in sand in Death Valley National Park, and the episode covers the early clues (guidebooks, film, a Treasure Island Hotel stay, the Warm Springs Mine logbook), the failed 1996 search, popular theories (staged disappearance, China Lake Naval Weapon Center, criminals), and how amateur desert explorer Tom Mahood found the remains roughly nine miles south of the van in 2009 after reasoning through the family's route and mindset. The episode ends with listener mail about The Far Side.

segments.title: Introduction and the missing family
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the Death Valley Germans case: a blended German family who vanished in July 1996 after renting a minivan for a California and Nevada trip. The family's members and itinerary are described, along with the van's rental and the missed flight home.

segments.title: Alert, discovery of the van, and Death Valley's heat
segments.summary: Interpol issues an alert after the family misses their flight. A ranger finds the abandoned Plymouth Voyager with three flat tires in October 1996. Death Valley's extreme heat and heat-related deaths are discussed.

segments.title: Van contents and German tourism
segments.summary: Officials inspect the van, which was stuck in sand and had driven on flat tires. Items found include Bud Ice beers and a Seahorse Resort business card. The hosts note Death Valley's popularity with Germans, partly due to the author Karl May.

segments.title: Clues: guidebooks, film, bank wire, and the geologist cabin flag
segments.summary: Clues include German guidebooks sold at the Furnace Creek Visitor Center, undeveloped film showing the Los Angeles, Highway 1 and Las Vegas trip at the Treasure Island Hotel, an unclaimed wire of fifteen hundred dollars sent to the wrong bank, and an American flag from the Geologist Cabin in Death Valley.

segments.title: Logbook clue and the failed 1996 search
segments.summary: Rangers check hotels and logbooks, and the Warm Springs Mine logbook shows a note saying they were going over the pass. A four-day search in October 1996 with about 250 people finds only a Bud Ice bottle and a butt print about 1.7 miles from the van. The search is called off and the case goes cold.

segments.title: Popular theories about the disappearance
segments.summary: Theories discussed include a staged disappearance to escape a custody battle, criminals or psychopaths (with the Barker Ranch and Manson family mentioned), and a secret government plot tied to China Lake Naval Weapon Center.

segments.title: Tom Mahood introduced
segments.summary: Tom Mahood, a retired civil engineer and desert explorer from Orange, California, becomes interested in the case and becomes obsessed with solving it.

segments.title: Mahood's return to the site in 2009
segments.summary: Mahood first hears of the case in 2008, returns to the van site in 2009 with a camera, retraces the route, and documents his work on a blog.

segments.title: Reconstructing the family's route and mindset
segments.summary: Mahood reasons through the family's money and time pressures and the last sunset photo taken at Hanaupah Canyon. The family takes a shortcut toward Mengel Pass, is stopped by impassable terrain, and backtracks past the locked geologist cabin in extreme heat.

segments.title: Dry wash, stranded van, and the walk toward China Lake
segments.summary: The van gets stuck in sand in a dry creek bed after a wrong fork. Egbert is believed to have sat in the shade drinking a beer, then reasoned that the nearby China Lake base would have a perimeter fence and help, but there was no fence.

segments.title: Discovery of remains by Tom Mahood and Les Walker
segments.summary: Mahood and Les Walker search south and find an empty wine bottle, a page of a German daily planner, and then bones at the base of a cliff about nine miles from the van. Cornelia's wallet is found with them, and the bones are left in place as they are reported.

segments.title: Identification, missing children, and reflections
segments.summary: DNA testing matched the remains to Egbert. No remains of the children were confirmed, though a small shoe was found. The hosts reflect on the family's final days and on Mahood's work.

segments.title: Listener mail about The Far Side
segments.summary: Listener Pete writes about his love of Gary Larson's The Far Side and a cartoon his mom did not get. The hosts thank listeners and invite more mail.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts sign off and credit iHeartRadio.
